subject: Segregated inference plane — isolated networking and deployment review
messages:
From: Alex Park <alex.park@edgeworks.io>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Eng Team <eng@edgeworks.io>
Date: 2025-08-09T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Segregated inference plane + isolated networking — review request

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for taking a look. We're kicking off a private deployment evaluation for a customer PoC and want to validate a few assumptions with Redwood before we finalize the network and procurement requirements. High level: the customer requires an isolated inference data plane in their VPC/colo, strict egress controls (only outbound to a handful of Redwood endpoints via an HTTP proxy), audit logs retained 13 months, and proof of control-plane separation.

Attached is a brief environment summary (VPC CIDR, on-prem subnets, proxy IPs). Can you review and confirm a recommended topology for:
- control-plane connection pattern (PrivateLink / VPN / dedicated interconnect)
- data-plane placement and egress design (proxy, NAT, TLS termination)
- where logs/metrics live and retention options for SOC2 evidence

Timeline: we'd like Redwood's alignment by EOD Tuesday (2025-08-12) so procurement can finalize language.

Thanks — happy to hop on a short call if useful.

--
Alex Park
Principal Engineer, EdgeWorks Solutions
alex.park@edgeworks.io

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Park <alex.park@edgeworks.io>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-08-09T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Segregated inference plane + isolated networking — review request

Alex — thanks for the clear summary and timeline. Looping in Marcus (network/ops) and Kimberly (security/compliance) to confirm details.

Quick answers up front:
- Control plane: we recommend an mTLS-protected control-channel back to a Redwood control endpoint. For most customers we support AWS PrivateLink or a customer-managed site-to-site VPN; for colo customers a dedicated private interconnect is also supported. PrivateLink gives the cleanest egress profile for SOC2 evidence.
- Data plane: inference nodes live in your customer subnets (dedicated worker ASG / bare-metal racks). Egress should terminate through your customer-managed forward proxy. Redwood does not need to accept inbound connections to those nodes.
- Logs/metrics: observability (metrics/traces) can be pushed via TLS to a Redwood ingestion endpoint or buffered locally and shipped; retention policy for SaaS ingestion is configurable — for this engagement we can provide an audit bundle to satisfy 13-month retention.

I've attached a quickly sketched topology and a first-draft runbook (seginfra_topology_v1.drawio.png, runbook_v1.pdf). They're intentionally high-level; Marcus, would you add specifics on NAT/proxy patterns and any host-level hardening we should call out? Kimberly, can you confirm the audit evidence we can deliver without additional agent installs?

If helpful, propose a 30m sync tomorrow to walk the diagram.

Best,
Karthik
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai

Thanks Karthik — the sketches look helpful. A few follow-ups from the procurement and security leads: 

1) Egress enforcement: customer will only allow HTTPS outbound via a forward proxy at 10.10.254.5:3128. Can Redwood's data-plane agents support proxying all outbound control/telemetry through that IP, or do we need an intermediate NAT gateway?
2) TLS termination: customer insists TLS termination at the proxy; they cannot accept TLS passthrough for reasons related to internal IDS. Does Redwood require end-to-end mTLS for control-plane traffic, or is hop-to-hop acceptable if the proxy enforces TLS?
3) Audit artifacts: procurement asked for what evidence Redwood can provide for RPC-level call logs and token-level request logs. The ask is specifically: request/response metadata (no user PII) for 13 months.

Also including the procurement contact: procurement@edgeworks.io for any legal evidence requests.

--
Alex

Subject: Re: Segregated inference plane + isolated networking — deployment details and runbook

Alex — quick operational answers and a proposed pattern below. Where helpful I've called out 'must' vs 'recommended'.

1) Proxy vs NAT
- Must: all outbound control/telemetry traffic originate from the data-plane hosts and be allowed by your forward proxy (10.10.254.5:3128). Redwood's data-plane processes can be configured to honor an outbound HTTP(S)_PROXY environment. If the proxy allows CONNECT to target hostnames/ports we can use standard HTTPS over that connect.
- Recommended: use a small NAT gateway for non-proxy traffic (package updates, OS repos), but keep control/telemetry strictly via the proxy to simplify audits.

2) TLS and mTLS
- Must: customer-controlled proxy performs TLS termination per your policy. Redwood requires authenticated control-plane channels to prevent rogue control messages. Option A (preferred): proxy supports TCP CONNECT for TLS and allows mTLS passthrough — we maintain end-to-end mTLS. Option B (acceptable): proxy terminates TLS but the proxy forwards traffic to a local sidecar that re-establishes mTLS to Redwood control endpoints. Both patterns are supported; Option A gives the cleanest cryptographic chain for attestation.

3) Audit/log artifacts
- Redwood can deliver: request-level metadata (timestamp, route, model id, token counts, status codes), control-plane events (join/heartbeat/rollout IDs), and per-request non-PII hashes for reproducibility. We can provide a daily/exported bundle for 13 months via a secure share (S3 presigned link or encrypted drive).

4) Practical runbook items
- Network: create customer security group allowing outbound to the proxy and to Redwood PrivateLink CIDR if using PrivateLink.
- Host hardening: enable host firewall with egress-only rules to the proxy; disable inbound management ports.
- KV cache: store on local encrypted disk; do not egress model state off-prem.

Attachments: updated topology (seginfra_topology_v1.drawio.png), runbook link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1xS-example-runbook, and I've created JIRA ticket JIRA-OPS-4492 to track the final NAT/proxy policy.

Next steps: if you confirm the proxy can allow CONNECT and preserve TLS passthrough we can mark Option A as the default. Otherwise we'll schedule 30m to map the sidecar-proxy flow.

Cheers,
Marcus Lin
Sr. Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai

Perfect — Option A works for us (proxy allows CONNECT and preserves TLS passthrough). Procurement confirmed the 13-month audit bundle requirement is acceptable via an encrypted S3 share.

Let's lock in:
- Default: TLS passthrough via proxy (end-to-end mTLS to Redwood control endpoints)
- Data-plane egress: proxy 10.10.254.5:3128 (all control/telemetry).
- Action: Marcus to provide a short checklist for host hardening and firewall rules by COB 2025-08-13.

Appreciate the fast turnaround — will schedule the 30m sync for Thursday to finalize runbook language.

Thanks,
